newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's national oil company slams court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Romania's national oil company slams court ruling.

text.p: A Romanian court on Tuesday ruled on Tuesday that the state-run Romanian National Oil Company (CRP) violated laws on monopolies, but a senior company official said the decision would not affect its operations.
"The effect of the so-called court ruling on CRP is nil. We are not affected by it and our business will go on as usual," CRP general manager Mihail Georgescu told Reuters.
"Such allegations are groundless and they don't mean CRP is dissolved," he added.
Legal officials were unable to provide copies of the ruling by the Bucharest Court of Appeal.

But the company challenging the firm's status, General Trading & Investments Co SA (GTI), a main shareholder of the local Petrogas SA private oil company, said it had "suspended government decision number 540/1996 which established CRP as a state monopoly".
Last month, GTI accused CRP of monopolistic practices and filed a lawsuit with the Court of Appeal asking it to annul the government decision to create the holding.
It also complained the CRP had hindered its oil importing activity by blocking its access to the country's sole oil port, Constanta on the Black Sea.
The CRP, a holding grouping 12 state-owned refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies as well as an oil exploration company, has repeatedly denied the accusations.
Ian Deacon, the GTI's press officer, said the court ruling was final.
But sources with the Barristers' Association in Bucharest told Reuters the CRP had the "theoretical" option to lodge an appeal with the Supreme Court.
"According to my knowledge the CRP can go to the Supreme Court for an appeal," the source said.
The government says the CRP, created in July, is intended to provide funds to import much needed crude oil and to streamline exploration, refining, distribution and transport of oil.
But some analysts see the new holding as on old-style East Bloc bureaucratic conglomerate. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
